judgements.reason: The manuscript compares a no-kernel majority with committee-based kernel regimes and explicitly says a crowds-plus-tools baseline was not tested, so it does not isolate mechanical checks from committee attestation.
Table 1 uses Clopper-Pearson intervals with n=120 while Section 4.2 states that board conditions share 60 committee draws, so the independence and variance concerns are supported.
The bounded-checking description leaves the state abstraction, action semantics, and S2 liveness interpretation under-specified despite the central verification claim.
The paper mixes deterministic seat bounds, realized committee captures, and an independence-based error model while honest unsafe error was zero, so the conflation concern is valid.
Colluders received extra private instructions and the reported token counts include hidden reasoning, so the token-length difference is not isolated as a deception cost.
The detector was evaluated against a cell instructed to reuse a talking point and vote as a shared minority, so high F1 mainly shows recovery of the planted signature.
The manuscript cites a mutable branch, keeps raw logs on request, and leaves call accounting and rerun inclusion insufficiently specified, so the reproducibility concern is valid.
Finding 3 attributes nine blocked valid releases to eight honest refusals without an event-level breakdown, so the causal accounting is unclear.
The novelty claims rely on characterizations of recent work, admit inaccessible candidates, and include an internal reference-verification note, so the related-work concern is valid.
The reference list contains late-2026 arXiv identifiers, a future sprint date, and an editorial note to verify references, so the concern about unverified or hallucinated citations is supported.
Section 3.4 says colluders used a shared talking point and Appendix B.4 uses TF-IDF text similarity plus shared-minority voting, so the detector result is confounded by the adversary design.
The manuscript reports zero honest unsafe errors and only 14 or 16 herding exposures, so the honest-error and herding claims are underpowered as stated.
The paper itself says the 120 trials contain 60 independent draws and calls the Clopper-Pearson intervals optimistic, so the clustering concern is correct.
The colluder prompt includes extra conditional instructions, so comparing total output tokens to honest agents confounds deception with instruction complexity.
The checker is described as serializing and deduplicating SQLite states without specifying canonicalization or the basis for depth 6, so the concern is valid.
The manuscript's 24-versus-36 and 60-draw/1.7-SD statement mixes paired-trial counts with an independent-draw calculation, so the seat-unit accounting concern is valid.

Section 3.2 calls the specification independently written while Appendix A says the same team wrote it and the LLM statement says the same assistant implemented both, so the verification-transfer concern is supported.
Figure 2 and Finding 5 use total output tokens including hidden reasoning from agents with different instructions, so the deliberation-cost claim is confounded.
The detector combines TF-IDF similarity with shared-minority voting against a cell told to share a talking point, and no vote-only or text-only ablation is reported.
Table 1's Clopper-Pearson intervals are computed over 120 trials despite shared committee draws and repeated agents, so the clustering concern is valid.
The abstract and conclusion generalize from 50 agents, instructed cells, and rare herding exposures while the limitations acknowledge those bounds, so the overclaiming concern is valid.
Raw logs are only available on request, one stochastic sweep per model was used, and denominators such as 0/746 are not derived, so the reproducibility concern is valid.
The gap claim relies on characterizations of recent 2026 preprints and admits two candidates were inaccessible, so the related-work verification concern is valid.

revised_own_concerns.issue: The abstract and contribution language generalize a bounded one-case, three-seat, depth-6 check to the broader live system and to semantic safety.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: Narrow the abstract and contribution claims to the verified toy configuration and add a table mapping verified assumptions to live-test assumptions, listing unverified dimensions such as 7-seat committees, 50 agents, multi-case interleavings, and LLM parsing/retry behavior.

revised_own_concerns.issue: The main uncertainty estimates and the 1.7-standard-deviation statement treat dependent pooled trials, shared committee draws, and repeated agents as independent Bernoulli observations.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: Declare the independent sampling unit, report per-draw and per-condition counts, and use cluster-aware paired tests, cluster bootstrap, or mixed-effects logistic regression instead of nominal Clopper-Pearson intervals over 120 pooled trials.

revised_own_concerns.issue: The capture formula's honest-error independence and full colluder-compliance assumptions are not empirically tested because honest unsafe error was zero and colluder compliance was below 100%.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: Add sensitivity analyses for nonzero and correlated honest error, report exact intervals for compliance and honest error, and qualify all safety-bound claims as task-specific.

revised_own_concerns.issue: The claim that crowds cannot verify is architectural because voters were given no verification tool, yet it is presented as a broad empirical finding.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: Add a crowds-plus-tools baseline with signature verification or narrow the claim to crowds without verification tools cannot check HMAC-bound receipts in this design.

revised_own_concerns.issue: The deliberation-cost result compares honest and colluding agents under different private instructions and includes hidden reasoning tokens, so it may reflect instruction complexity rather than deception.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: Report visible-only token counts, add instruction-length-matched honest controls or concise-colluder conditions, and present the result as a role-conditioned association rather than a robust monitoring signal.

revised_own_concerns.issue: Reproducibility is limited by a mutable branch, raw logs available only on request, sparse detector tuning details, and apparently single stochastic sweeps per model.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: Archive a commit hash with sanitized raw logs, prompts, seeds, configuration files, detector outputs, and at least one repeated seed or bootstrap analysis, plus a detector threshold ablation.

revised_own_concerns.issue: Denominators and trial sets are not uniformly defined across Table 1 columns, and live denominators such as 0/746, 8/492, and 262 are not derived.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: Add footnotes or separate tables for each denominator, derive all reported counts, and for the hybrid regime state whether bounds are conditioned on the majority precondition.

revised_own_concerns.issue: S2 is described as liveness, but bounded finite-depth exploration cannot establish eventual release under arbitrary schedules.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: Define S2 as a bounded enablement or successful-admission property and state the scheduling assumptions explicitly.

revised_own_concerns.issue: The abstract's no-herding claim is based on only 14 and 16 exposure events with zero observed approvals.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: Temper the claim to no observed herding on a crisp task with rare exposures, and report exact intervals or a power analysis.

revised_own_concerns.issue: The references include late-2026 arXiv identifiers, inaccessible candidate papers, and an internal note to verify references, undermining the related-work positioning and novelty claims.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: Audit every citation, remove or replace unverifiable entries, verify all arXiv identifiers, and qualify any novelty claims that depend on unchecked sources.

new_concerns.issue: The evaluation lacks a majority-plus-mechanical-checks baseline without a committee, so the benefit of separation-of-powers committee governance is not isolated from ordinary kernel mechanical checks.
new_concerns.suggested_fix: Replay majority decisions through the kernel's integrity, policy, uniqueness, and audit checks without requiring committee approval, and report safety, throughput, and cost alongside the hybrid regime.

new_concerns.issue: The detector's near-perfect F1 is confounded by the planted shared talking point and shared-minority voting, and no ablation or adaptive-colluder control is reported.
new_concerns.suggested_fix: Report vote-only, text-only, and combined detector performance, add benign-minority and paraphrasing-colluder controls, and narrow the claim to detection of the tested planted-cell behavior.

new_concerns.issue: Finding 1's seat-bound accounting is not auditable because paired-trial counts, independent-draw counts, and the reported 1.7-standard-deviation calculation appear to use different units.
new_concerns.suggested_fix: Publish per-condition capturable counts, declare whether the unit is a trial, target case, or independent committee draw, clarify nesting across boards, and recompute the deviation on one declared unit.

new_concerns.issue: The claim of an independently written specification is contradicted by Appendix A's same-team statement and the LLM usage statement describing the same assistant implementing both kernel and checker.
new_concerns.suggested_fix: Correct the independence claim, discuss common-mode specification error, and either provide an independent specification review or narrow the verification contribution accordingly.

new_concerns.issue: The bounded checker's SQLite state canonicalization, deduplication method, and depth-6 sufficiency horizon are not specified, leaving open whether deduplication preserves all behaviorally relevant state.
new_concerns.suggested_fix: Specify the canonical state representation used for hashing, describe excluded metadata, justify depth 6, and optionally add a small competing-execution or two-case check.

new_concerns.issue: The attribution of nine blocked valid releases under unanimity to eight honest refusals lacks an event-level breakdown.
new_concerns.suggested_fix: Provide a breakdown of blocked valid releases by honest refusal, colluder refusal, abstention, parsing or transport failure, and other causes, allowing multiple causes per case.
